the HIV-1 Rev NES interacts with FG nucleoporins in the yeast two-hybrid assay, that Rev NES mutants that do not export RNA in yeast also fail to interact with FG nucleoporin, and that FG nucleoporins inhibit the export of Rev protein and U snRNA from Xenopus oocytes.
the HIV Rev protein and its NES are able to interact with several different FG repeat-containing nucleoportins in yeast and mammal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nucleoporins in RNA export.
understanding the mechanism by which the human immunodeficiency type virus Rev protein interacts with the nuclear pore complex to export viral RNA.
the role of nucleoporins in the export of Rev protein and RNA and the mechanism of Rev function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Rev protein is a nucleoporin-binding protein, and this binding is important for its export function.
the FG repeat domains of nucleoporin proteins play a critical role in export of Rev and U small nuclear RNA, as well as other cellular RNAs.

the nucleoporin FG repeats are involved in Rev protein and Rev-dependent RNA export from the nucleus, and that the FG repeat domains of nucleoporins may play a more general role in the export of cellular mRNAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rev NES interacts with multiple FG repeat domains of nucleoporins and that these interactions are required for Rev-mediated and cellular export of RNAs from the nucleus.

the nucleoporins that interact with the Rev NES are involved in both nuclear export of Rev protein and Rev-dependent nuclear export of RNA, and that the interaction of Rev with these nucleoporins is important for Rev function.
the Rev protein contains an NES which interacts with a subset of FG nucleoporin repeats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FG nucleoporins are not only involved in nuclear protein import, but they are also involved in nuclear RNA export.
the FG nucleoporin repeats are not only involved in protein import but also in export.
